advices.diagnosis: The class has a critical LCOM4 of 4, meaning its methods are largely isolated – each getter touches a distinct private attribute, so the method‑attribute graph splits into many components. The class is essentially a data holder with only one real behavior (is_premium). It also has a perfect DAM of 1.0, indicating all attributes are private, which contributes to the low cohesion. No internal dependencies (DCC=0) and modest method count (NOM=5) keep the other metrics low, but the high LCOM4 signals a design smell: the class is over‑encapsulated for a simple data structure.

suggestions.title: Replace getters with public fields via a dataclass
suggestions.sketch:
Convert the class to a @dataclass with public attributes and keep only the business method:
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Customer:
    customer_id: int
    name: str
    email: str
    tier: str = "standard"

    def is_premium(self) -> bool:
        return self.tier == "premium"
```
Remove the explicit getter methods; callers will access attributes directly (e.g., cust.name).

advices.risk_notes: Existing code that calls the getter methods (customer_id(), name(), etc.) will break and must be updated to use attribute access. If the class is part of a public API, this change is a breaking change and may require a deprecation period or wrapper methods to preserve compatibility.
